answer.rationale: p99 latency is degrading on the write path, isolated to the primary region, and a release went out 2 hours ago — the working hypotheses are bad release, regional issue, or capacity. With only ONE intervention, memory_b1 is the highest-leverage prior: a release rollback previously cleared a checkout error spike without customer impact, which directly maps to this signature (recent release + write-path regression + settlement-heavy traffic). Rolling back has the best chance of restoring write availability immediately while preserving customer writes, and can be staged safely. Regional failover (memory_b2) is the backup if the rollback doesn't move the needle; I don't want to failover first because shifting settlement writes mid-peak adds risk if the cause is the build. Circuit breaker / capacity / read replicas don't address a recent deployment and would waste the single-intervention slot. Verifying memory_b1 before committing to confirm the prior rollback pattern held cleanly and the build classification (bad vs. environmental) was sound.
